CHIEF COMPLAINT
Referral from emergency room for evaluation of esophagitis.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a new patient referred from the ER for evaluation of esophagitis. Three months ago in early October 2020, she experienced acute onset central chest pain located behind her breastbone. The pain was sharp in quality and made her feel like she was having a heart attack. The pain occurred randomly and was not present upon waking. The chest discomfort lasted four days and was exacerbated by eating. She also experienced associated difficulty swallowing. Despite attempting various interventions at home, the pain did not improve, prompting her to seek emergency care. At the ER, an EKG and blood tests were performed, both of which were normal. No medications were prescribed during the ER visit. The ER staff attributed the symptoms to a possible gastrointestinal etiology and referred her to gastroenterology. Her chest pain and difficulty swallowing resolved approximately three days after the ER visit. She has remained asymptomatic since that time, though she reports a persistent feeling that something is wrong. When questioned about heartburn or indigestion, she is uncertain as she has no prior history of heartburn. The patient notes that she was undergoing a stressful job transition at the time of symptom onset.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports attempting to lose weight. Denies abdominal pain. Bowel movements are normal. No history of heartburn, though uncertain if she experienced it during the acute episode.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Uterine fibroids
Anemia
Status post cholecystectomy several years ago

MEDICATIONS
Not discussed.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Denies family history of gastrointestinal problems.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Stressful job transition occurring around the time of symptom onset. Currently attempting to lose weight.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Abdomen: Lower abdomen without pain or tenderness to palpation. Upper abdominal quadrants with mild tenderness to light palpation, symmetrical bilaterally. Remainder of exam appears normal.

RESULTS
EKG (ER): normal
Blood tests (ER): normal
Cardiac workup: normal

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Patient with history of acute chest pain with associated dysphagia occurring three months ago in early October 2020. Differential diagnosis includes GERD, dyspepsia, esophagitis, musculoskeletal etiologies, and anxiety. Cardiac etiology has been ruled out by normal EKG and cardiac workup performed in the ER. Clinical assessment is that patient likely had an anxiety attack related to her job transition, with possible contribution from musculoskeletal etiologies. Patient has remained asymptomatic since the acute episode.

Discussed options of upper endoscopy (EGD) versus conservative management with symptom monitoring. Explained that if esophagitis had been present, it would likely have healed by this time given the three-month duration of complete symptom resolution, and EGD may not reveal active findings. Patient elected to defer EGD and self-monitor for symptom recurrence. Patient instructed to contact the office if she experiences any recurrent chest pain, additional gastrointestinal symptoms, or other concerning symptoms, at which point EGD can be performed if indicated. To follow up as needed for any other gastrointestinal complaints.
